changelog:
Session memory capture finishes again, and recall builds its embedding index on its own.

Fixes: a host that runs each Claude session in its own systemd scope (T3 Code) stops that scope when the session ends, which killed the capture child mid-call (7 of 325 captures finished in one measurement). Hook background work (capture, the index run, the daily log and curator) now starts through systemd-run --user --scope when the hook runs inside such a scope; AGENTS_SCOPE_ESCAPE=off turns that off. A project whose embedding index was never built now builds it: the recall hook starts the throttled background index whenever the index lags the corpus, also when the prompt fell back to keyword-only.

Features: capture is incremental. A session that ends several times (a resumed thread) sends only what it added since its last pass, instead of the whole transcript each time or nothing after the first pass.

Migration: none required. If recall is mostly keyword-only, keep the embedding model loaded on its server (OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE): a prompt's recall waits 400 ms and a cold model load takes seconds.

--- v6.17 ---
Epic checklists from the planning pipeline now carry verify: bindings, so a /run-todo on them proves its criteria.

Features: /create-project-epics-todo writes each acceptance criterion as a checkbox bullet: the backlog text verbatim, then a verify: command that names the test file the story will create, or a [manual]/[CI-pending] tag. Its Validate step runs ac-verify list (parse only) and checks that no criterion is left without a binding or tag. /run-todo Phase 0 counts open stories that have no verify: bindings and asks once: add the bindings first, or run those stories all-manual. A headless run records the choice and continues.

Fixes: the epic template's plain-bullet acceptance criteria were never parsed as criteria (only Tasks checkboxes were), so every epic story sealed as all-manual.

Migration: none required. Existing epic checklists still run. /run-todo now warns about them, and /todo can add their bindings.

--- v6.16 ---
/do fits content work, and run records count only what the run did.

Features: handoff-path.js write takes --stamp so a run's handoff reuses its plan's stamp. A content-only change outside the gated app (seed data, course text) commits with an audited skip that names the check that verified it, and stays with Main Agent whatever its length (LOC counts code only). Prose that states policy, authority, commands or numbers someone acts on (a course, a runbook, release notes) gets a real review against its sources, not a light read. Finishing a branch reuses a gate receipt that already covers the branch tip, and keeps the merged branch's newest handoff on the base branch.

Fixes: run-record wave needs --story only for a /run-todo run (an ad-hoc /do drops it again); a gate run is logged only for a `node ... gate.js` invocation that runs a leg, not a command that merely names gate.js; session-handoff and /do agree that the handoff is written before the commit; a runtime without TaskCreate tracks the stages in the plan file; a headless browser fallback when the Playwright installer refuses the OS; corrected counts (50 workflows, 24 knowledge skills, 17 hook handlers) and the secret-scan gap note; the v6.15 note now says the detect-only job reads the last local gate result.

Migration: none required.
